title: Review on progress of rare earth molecule-based functional materials in 2025
claim: Soft S, Se, and Te donors form luminescent Ce(III) complexes outside the usual O/N ligand set; sulfur coordination stabilizes Ce 5d orbitals and red-shifts emission, while bulky N-alkyl groups increase ligand-field splitting toward deep-red emission beyond 700 nm.
explanation: The review presents Se- and Te-coordinated luminescent Ce(III) complexes as the first of their type and attributes the red shift to covalent, polar S–Ce bonding. Large steric hindrance that enforces a mononuclear structure is specifically linked to stronger ligand-field splitting and wavelengths above 700 nm.
scope: Luminescent Ce(III) complexes with soft chalcogen donors, especially S-coordinated systems whose N-alkyl bulk is varied.
conditions: Soft S/Se/Te coordination; alkyl substitution on ligand nitrogen atoms.
caveats: The deep-red >700 nm result is tied to the sterically enforced mononuclear structure in the cited S-donor example, not to every soft-donor Ce complex.
